Jordan — thanks for pulling this together. Quick pass below (inline):

> Top asks:
> - review the short playbook and call out any missing focus areas by EOD

Done — playbook looks good. Two additions I think are important for the Sr level:
- Product strategy at model-level: candidate should be able to articulate a 6–12 month roadmap decision that balances model upgrades, quantization, and customer SLAs.
- Experiment design + metrics: beyond pure A/B, they should define guardrails for regressions (per-customer thresholds, golden prompt sets).

> - Where should we anchor scoring for product sense vs. execution vs. inference-specific tradeoffs?

Proposed weights (quick): Product sense 35%, Inference tradeoffs 30%, Execution (delivery/operationalization) 25%, Collaboration/leadership 10%. Open to pushback.

> - Agree on three anchor questions for the bar-raiser

My suggested anchors:
1) "Describe a time you had to choose between model quality and latency/cost — how did you decide and measure success?"
2) "Walk me through a rollout where something regressed in production — how did you detect & respond?"
3) "Given this product problem (see candidate pack), what would you de-prioritize and why?"

Also: add a short interview rubric cheat-sheet (1-pager) that interviewers can print. Happy to draft it if you want.

—Marissa

Great thread — adding a pragmatic leveling matrix (see leveling_matrix_PM_vs_SrPM.xlsx) and a short note on what "inference judgment" looks like at Redwood. Inline highlights: 

- Leveling matrix highlights:
  * PM: identifies latency/cost as requirements, collaborates with infra to scope tradeoffs.
  * Sr PM: defines service-level cost/latency objectives, creates routing/fallback policies, and owns regression SLAs with SLO burn-down plans.

- Interview probes I recommend for the bar-raiser to focus on:
  1) Depth of system tradeoffs understanding (second-order effects of caching, KV cache sizing, batching).
  2) Evidence of ownership on cross-functional rollout (did they write the playbook, or just follow it?).
  3) Ability to convert ambiguous requirements into measurable acceptance criteria.

I also recommend we standardize debrief outputs: 3 bullets for signal (what we saw), 2 bullets for risk, and a binary hire/no-hire recommendation with confidence level (low/medium/high). If we adopt that template, debriefs will be faster and more consistent.

-Markus
Markus Klein
